intro: Kuwait grew from a small trading port into an oil-rich state, and survived invasion by Iraq in 1990.

chapters.title: A trading port
text: Failaka Island had a Bronze Age settlement and later a Greek outpost founded under Alexander the Great. In the 1700s families from Arabia settled Kuwait town, and in 1756 they chose the Al Sabah family to lead them; it still rules today.
Kuwaitis built wooden dhows and sailed to India and East Africa, and dived for pearls.

chapters.title: Protection and oil
text: To stay independent of the Ottomans, Kuwait signed a protection treaty with Britain in 1899. Oil was discovered at Burgan in 1938, one of the largest oil fields in the world. Kuwait became independent in 1961.

chapters.title: Invasion and liberation
text: On 2 August 1990 Saddam Hussein's Iraq invaded and annexed Kuwait. A US-led coalition of many countries drove Iraqi forces out in February 1991. Retreating troops set over 600 oil wells on fire, which burned for months.

highlight.title: The Gulf War
highlight.text: The 1991 liberation was one of the largest military coalitions since World War Two.

keyTerms.meaning: To take over another country's land and make it your own.
